title: Data and Application Engineer
description:
Overview

Data and Application Engineer role at Apollo.

Your Role

As a Data and Application Engineer, you will be working closely with colleagues across the business to deliver the data, applications, and services they need. This hands-on role will see you design and develop data pipelines, model and transform data for ease of use, and automate key business processes. You will also play a vital role in supporting data quality, timeliness, and governance, ensuring Apollo’s data strategy continues to evolve and thrive.

What you will do

  • Build strong relationships with stakeholders to understand requirements and shape effective data solutions.
  • Design and implement data models and ETL pipelines aligned with our data platform principles.
  • Develop, maintain, and enhance applications and automation tools that support business operations.
  • Act as a subject matter expert in Azure Data Factory, Azure Databricks, Unity Catalogue, and SQL Server.
  • Apply best practice to data quality, lineage, and governance, ensuring compliance and security standards are met.
  • Contribute to agile delivery processes, code control, and quality assurance standards.
  • Monitor, troubleshoot, and improve existing data sets and processes, identifying opportunities to enhance coverage and performance.
  • Support colleagues through testing, training, and knowledge transfer, enabling them to fully utilise data solutions.

What we are looking for

  • Proven experience in data engineering and solution design.
  • Strong technical expertise in Azure Data Factory, Azure Databricks, Unity Catalogue, and SQL Server.
  • Practical knowledge of data modelling and ETL pipeline development.
  • Ability to profile and analyse raw data, operational systems, and business processes.
  • Hands-on coding and development skills, with a focus on quality, testing, and standards.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to explain complex solutions clearly.
  • A collaborative, problem-solving mindset with a focus on continuous improvement and innovation.

What you will get in return

Our compensation package is designed to attract top talent. In addition to a fair and attractive salary, this role offers a discretionary bonus and a comprehensive range of benefits, including 31 days of annual leave, a non-contributory pension and private medical insurance.

Our Commitment to Inclusion

Apollo is a growing and diverse team of empowered and passionate experts who focus on bringing innovation, data driven decision making and collaboration to every relationship and every risk. To meet the needs of a demanding global insurance market, we need a diverse workforce that truly understands the international communities we serve.

That is why we're focused on developing diverse talent at every level; inclusion and diversity means more to us than just chasing a target and we are committed to supporting and celebrating difference. Our people are at the heart of our business which is why we value the diversity of thought and talent of every member of our team.

We offer a range of support and run a programme of events and training that recognise the challenges and opportunities relating to diversity.

Hybrid & flexible working

At Apollo, hybrid and flexible working is fully embraced and we do not see the benefit of presenteeism. We understand that no two colleagues are alike, and as such we support the ability to remain agile and achieve a home and work balance to best suit business and personal commitments.

Supporting your application

Apollo are committed to ensuring an inclusive and supportive recruitment experience for everyone. Our process includes both virtual (Microsoft Teams) and in-person interviews. If there’s anything we can do to make your experience more comfortable or accessible, please let us know.

You can share any adjustments or support you may need in advance or on the day with Clear Talents

Thank you!

title: Data Engineer - Group
description:
CoreGo is an event technology company powering large-scale events and festivals. Our seamless payment and access control solutions ensure smooth operations and effortless experiences for attendees and organizers alike. Combining technical innovation with deep industry expertise, we help bring ambitious live experiences to life.

Job Description

As a Data Engineer, you'll join a growing team and takeon a substantial role in developing and operating CoreGo's data platform with real influence over development. You'll work closely with product management, software developers, and our existing data/analytics team. It's a chance to make a lasting mark on the technology behind some of Europe's biggest live events.

You'll take ownership of CoreGo's data platform on Databricks — developing it, keeping it running reliably, and growing it as our data and AI needs evolve. Day to day, this includes:

Developing and evolving the platform's ingestion, lakehouse architecture, transformation pipelines, and orchestration

Building and maintaining the data models and pipelines that power analytics, reporting, and machine learning workloads across CoreGo Cloud (payments, access control, network, POS)

Maintaining strong data quality, testing, and CI/CD practices across the platform

Defining and evolving access control, data governance, and security standards (e.g. Unity Catalog)

On the operations side, you'll:

Run the platform in production — monitoring, incident response, and performance/cost optimization (cluster and compute management)

Extend the platform with new data products, pipelines, and use cases as CoreGo's data and AI roadmap grows

Collaborate with product management and developers to integrate data/ML outputs into business processes and customer-facing products

Own data reliability and scalability as usage and event volumes grow

Degree in Computer Science, Data Engineering, or another relevant technical field

3+ years of hands-on data engineering experience designing and building data pipelines

Practical experience with Databricks (or an equivalent Spark-based platform), including PySpark and workflow orchestration

Experience with infrastructure-as-code and DevOps practices for data platforms

Experience with cloud platforms, ideally Microsoft Azure

Understanding of data security and governance best practices

Strong analytical thinking, attention to detail, and ability to manage your own workload

Ability to work independently and take initiative, while fitting well within the team

Proficiency in English

  • Work with meaningful, growth-driven solutions— our technology powers seamless payment and access experiences for hundreds of thousands of people at some of Europe's most memorable live events, giving you a dynamic, forward-looking environment to build and grow in.
  • Take on real ownership— you'll have genuine influence over how our data platform evolves, with the trust and space to shape decisions rather than just execute on them.
  • Grow with an international team— you'll collaborate closely with experienced colleagues, contributing to CoreGo's international journey.
  • Enjoy a culture that balances ambition and authenticity— we're professional, driven, and down-to-earth. We take our work seriously, without taking ourselves too seriously.

Practical Information

This is a permanent, full-time position. Start date is flexible and will be discussed individually.

We are looking for a person based in Finland who can work remotely while also being available to visit our Helsinki office on an occasional basis.

Considered an Advantage

  • Databricks Certified Data Engineer Professional (or equivalent certification)
  • Familiarity with ML models and tooling
  • Experience with API- and microservice-oriented architectures

title: Optical Engineer
description:
Social networking, machine learning, and big data analytics demand ever-increasing network connectivity. RANOVUS, with operations in Ottawa, Canada, Nuremberg, Germany, and San Jose, USA, is a solution provider for the next generation data center infrastructures. We aim to deliver advanced technology that minimizes environmental impact through lower power dissipation.

Working with world class fabrication partners, RANOVUS is the leader in the application of unique new technologies to fiber-optic communications products for data centers.

We are seeking a motivated and talented Optical Engineer to join our Optical System Integration/ Verification team. The successful candidate would implement and test electrical and optical hardware/system for leading-edge optical communication modules for customer delivery.

Responsibilities include:
• Collaborate with multi-functional groups (photonics, hardware and software) to bring-up, validate, debug, calibrate, optimize and characterize optical engine performance.
• Understand product requirements, define test objectives, and develop detailed optical performance test plans that outline test strategies, scope, configurations, deliverables, and schedules.
• Establish complex lab setups using various high-speed electrical/optical lab equipment (oscilloscope, network analyzer, spectrum analyzer, BERT, etc.).
• Design, develop and maintain automated test scripts to adjust operating conditions of the device and capture the measurement data.
• Root-causes analysis of optical performance issues through lab experimentation and collaboration with design teams.
• Create test reports that summarize test results, key findings, and bug fixes.
• Support interworking between AE and the R&D team and the marketing team.
• Collaborate with external instrument vendors for equipment procurement and ensure seamless software and control integration.

Requirements:
• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Optical Engineering, Physics, Electrical Engineering, or a related field.
• 2 to 5 years relevant work experience on optical systems or opto-electronics devices (lasers, detectors, modulators, transceivers).
• Knowledge of optical systems and components, digital communication systems, HW, PCB, SW/FW.
• Experience in Python or Matlab script languages.
• Experience in a lab environment including troubleshooting issues.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills

Desirable skills:
• Knowledge of very high-speed interconnects (electrical and optical) for Ethernet, PCIe/CXL etc.
• Exposure to programming and debugging embedded software on microcontrollers.

If you have a passion for technology and innovation and want to be part of a team pushing the boundaries, we encourage you to apply.

Ranovus is an equal opportunity employer.

title: Coordinator II (Academic Programs Coordinator)
description:
Job Summary:

The Department of Health Policy and Management (HPM) is committed to training and inspiring the next generation of health care leaders. Our students and faculty are passionate about making the world a better place by improving health and health care. We work on compelling and important problems, from making the delivery of care safer and more efficient, to expanding health insurance coverage and eliminating disparities, to designing and improving the performance of entire health systems.

Job-Specific Responsibilities:

  • The Academic Programs Coordinator provides administrative, technical, and analytical support to the Assistant Director of Academic Programs and Student Services in the Department of Health Policy and Management (HPM) and to the Faculty Director of Academic Programs in HPM, who also serves as the School's Senior Associate Dean for Educational Programs.
  • In this highly student-facing role, the Coordinator must demonstrate excellent judgment, strong organizational skills, and outstanding written and verbal communication. As the primary point of contact for prospective and current students in HPM's academic programs, the Coordinator responds to inquiries related to recruitment, admissions, technical support, course advising, and navigating the overall student experience at Harvard Chan.
  • The successful candidate will be comfortable working with a variety of student information, admissions, and learning management systems, including SOPHAS, my.harvard, and Canvas, and will provide guidance and technical support to faculty and teaching assistants using these platforms. The Coordinator also tracks academic program expenditures and maintains student records, degree audit information, and other program documentation.
  • The Coordinator develops, coordinates, and distributes a wide range of academic communications and materials, including the HPM Department Handbook, advisor resources, marketing materials, and electronic communications for students and faculty. Responsibilities also include preparing mailings to alumni and current students, administering the annual alumni survey, collecting marketing and competitive benchmarking data, and continuously identifying opportunities to improve the quality and effectiveness of program content and communications.
  • This position conducts data analysis and prepares reports related to academic programs, including admissions metrics, student exit surveys, alumni feedback, program evaluations, and other ad hoc analyses to support program assessment and decision-making.
  • The Coordinator also supports faculty, instructors, and teaching assistants in all aspects of curriculum planning and course administration, including CEP review, syllabus preparation, and Canvas course site management.
  • Serving as a primary liaison with departments across the School—including Admissions, the Registrar, Financial Services, the Office for Education, and the Office for Diversity and Inclusion—the Coordinator collaborates closely with the Office for Education to implement admissions processes and degree auditing for students in the Health Policy and Health Management tracks of the MPH program.
  • Working in partnership with the Assistant Director, the Coordinator plans and supports departmental programming for students, including orientation activities, cohort meetings, and social events. The Coordinator also participates in and supports School-wide events such as Admitted Students Day, Orientation, Graduation, Open Houses, and other academic programs, and performs additional duties as assigned.

title: Quality Assurance Technician – Training Available
description:
Are You the Person Who Notices What Everyone Else Misses?

Royalton or Bethel, VT | Competitive Hourly Pay + Shift Differential + Regular Overtime

You may be qualified for a technical career you've never considered.

I'm looking for people in and around Central Vermont who are detail-oriented, careful, consistent, and naturally notice when something isn't quite right.

You do not need "Quality Assurance Technician" on your résumé.

You might currently work in:

  • Manufacturing or production
  • Machine operation
  • Medical or dental support
  • Pharmacy technician work
  • Laboratory work
  • Automotive service or inspection
  • Electronics assembly
  • Food or beverage manufacturing
  • Inventory or receiving
  • Shipping and fulfillment
  • CNC or precision manufacturing
  • Calibration or testing
  • Another job where accuracy and attention to detail matter

Or maybe your current job doesn't fit neatly into any of those categories.

That's okay.

What matters is whether you're someone who pays attention to details, follows procedures, keeps accurate records, catches mistakes, and takes pride in getting things right.

Not Sure Your Skills Transfer?

Don't automatically rule yourself out — and don't worry about a résumé yet.

Great Bay Staffing created a short Skills Transfer Review specifically for people who may have the right abilities for Quality Assurance but have never held a Quality Technician job.

Tell us what you do now, what you're responsible for getting right, and the kinds of things you check, inspect, measure, verify, or document.

We'll personally review your experience to determine whether the skills you already have could transfer into this opportunity.

Start your Skills Transfer Review here:

No résumé required. It's not a job application.

What Could You Move Into?

I'm recruiting for Quality Assurance Technician positions with an established precision manufacturing and injection molding company in Royalton and Bethel, Vermont.

Quality Technicians help ensure precision-manufactured products meet exact specifications and quality standards before they leave the production floor.

The work includes:

  • Inspecting precision-manufactured parts
  • Learning to use measurement tools such as micrometers and calipers
  • Following Quality Assurance Requirements and Control Plans
  • Collecting samples and documenting inspection results
  • Maintaining accurate quality records
  • Identifying defects and inconsistencies
  • Verifying required production and quality procedures
  • Investigating quality issues
  • Working with production teams to solve problems
  • Helping ensure products meet demanding customer and regulatory standards

Previous quality or manufacturing experience is helpful.

But it isn't required for the right person.

What Makes Someone Good at Quality?

Quality is about more than inspecting parts.

It's a way of working.

Maybe you're the person who notices a number doesn't match.

Maybe "close enough" bothers you when you know there's a correct way to do something.

Maybe you're good at following detailed procedures, keeping accurate records, or catching errors before they become bigger problems.

Maybe you're willing to speak up when something doesn't look right.

Quality systems and measurement tools can be taught. Attention to detail is much harder to teach.

That's why I'm interested in talking to people outside the traditional Quality Assurance talent pool.

The Schedule

These are 12-hour rotating shifts, typically working 3 or 4 days per week.

Current schedules may include:

A Shift: Sunday–Tuesday + every other Wednesday, 6AM–6PM

B Shift: Sunday–Tuesday + every other Wednesday, 6PM–6AM

C Shift: Thursday–Saturday + every other Wednesday, 6AM–6PM

D Shift: Thursday–Saturday + every other Wednesday, 6PM–6AM

Both day and night shift opportunities may be available.

Shift placement depends on current openings.

Why Consider It?

  • Competitive hourly compensation
  • Shift differential where applicable
  • Regular overtime opportunities
  • Medical, dental and vision benefits
  • Retirement benefits
  • Clean, climate-controlled production facilities
  • Training and continuing education
  • Long-term career development
  • Opportunities to advance within a stable global organization

I'm Not Sure I'm Qualified

That's exactly why I'm running this ad.

Don't disqualify yourself just because your current résumé doesn't say "Quality Assurance."

If you're good at catching mistakes, following detailed procedures, inspecting or measuring things, keeping accurate records, or simply making sure things are done correctly, let us determine whether your experience could transfer.

You have two options:

Already interested in the Quality Assurance Technician position? Use the Apply Now button on this posting.

Not sure whether your experience qualifies? Complete the Great Bay Staffing Skills Transfer Review:

No résumé required for the review. Not a job application. Just tell us what you know how to do.

title: Service Charge & Revenue Director (Q - CO)
description:
Jasara Program Management Company (Jasara PMC) is a leading Joint Venture between Public Investment Fund (PIF), Jacobs, and Saudi Aramco, established to deliver world-class program management services across the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Jasara plays a key role in supporting the realization of Saudi Vision 2030, particularly in delivering giga-projects and large-scale infrastructure developments.

We are seeking a Service Charge Director to join JASARA PMC. The role responsibility is own the city-wide service charge framework, governance and operating model, ensuring service charges, cost recovery mechanisms and revenue opportunities are consistently identified, evaluated, governed and aligned with City Operations, Asset Management and district operating requirements.

The Service Charges & Revenue Director is accountable for establishing and maintaining the city-wide service charge framework, governance model, charging methodologies and revenue optimization approach across the Qiddiya City operating model. The role provides city-wide coordination and assurance across Estate Management, City Operations, Asset

Management, Finance, districts, operators and delivery teams to ensure operational costs, common area services and shared infrastructure are appropriately understood, allocated and recoverable where applicable.The role acts as the owner and custodian of the city-wide service charge model, providing governance, oversight and assurance over cost allocation methodologies, cost recovery structures and service charge assumptions. The position also leads the identification and evaluation of revenue opportunities across city assets, facilities, infrastructure and common areas, ensuring opportunities are assessed from operational, commercial and asset-management perspectives before recommendations are escalated to senior management. The role directs the Service Charges & Revenue Senior Manager and works closely with Lifecycle Planning, Finance, Asset Management, City Operations and district stakeholders to support long-term operational sustainability, financial resilience and value optimization across the city operating model.

Key Responsibilities

1. Service Charge Framework and Governance

• Establish and maintain the city-wide service charge framework, governance structure, policies, methodologies and

operating principles across applicable assets, facilities, services and districts.

• Develop and maintain service charge allocation principles, recharge methodologies, cost categorization structures and

governance requirements.

• Ensure service charge arrangements are transparent, equitable, auditable and aligned with approved operational and

commercial objectives.

• Own annual service charge review processes, governance controls, methodology updates and assurance requirements.

• Develop policy recommendations relating to service charge methodologies and governance arrangements for leadership

review and approval.

• Ensure service charge approaches remain aligned with operating models, asset ownership structures, operational

responsibilities and district requirements.

• Promote consistency in charging practices and cost recovery principles across the wider city operating model.

• Provide leadership reporting on service charge governance effectiveness, risks, issues and improvement opportunities.

2. City-Wide Service Charge Model Ownership

• Own and maintain the city-wide service charge model and supporting governance arrangements.

• Coordinate inputs from Asset Management, City Operations, Finance, districts, operators and external advisors to ensure

model integrity and consistency.

• Review and challenge charging assumptions, allocation methodologies, cost drivers and model outputs to ensure robust

decision making.

• Ensure common area services, shared infrastructure, public realm assets and city-wide services are appropriately

reflected within service charge calculations.

• Maintain transparent assumptions, supporting evidence and governance records for all significant model decisions.

• Monitor model effectiveness and ensure assumptions evolve in line with city growth, asset commissioning and operational

maturity.

• Develop management information, dashboards and reporting outputs to support leadership review and decision making.

• Support periodic reviews of service charge affordability, allocation fairness and cost recovery effectiveness.

3. Revenue Strategy and Commercial Opportunity Assessment

• Lead the identification and evaluation of revenue-generating opportunities associated with city assets, infrastructure,

facilities, services and common areas.

• Assess emerging opportunities that support operational sustainability and maximize value from city-owned or city-

managed assets.

• Coordinate commercial evaluations of potential revenue streams, recovery mechanisms and value-generation initiatives.

• Develop business case inputs, financial assessments and strategic recommendations for leadership consideration.

• Ensure revenue opportunities are evaluated against operational requirements, customer experience expectations and

long-term city objectives.

• Maintain visibility of revenue-generating initiatives across districts, operators and asset portfolios.

• Monitor market developments and emerging trends that may create future revenue opportunities for the city.

• Provide evidence-based recommendations regarding potential revenue generation, value optimization and cost recovery

enhancement.

4. OPEX and Lifecycle Cost Integration

• Coordinate operating expenditure inputs with City Operations, operators, Finance and Asset Management stakeholders.

• Ensure service charge assumptions appropriately reflect approved service levels, operational requirements and operating

delivery models.

• Work closely with the Asset Lifecycle Planning & Integration Director to incorporate lifecycle forecasts, renewal obligations

and long-term asset funding requirements into service charge considerations.

• Ensure lifecycle cost impacts and renewal pressures are visible during service charge reviews and cost recovery

assessments.

• Coordinate discussions regarding maintenance obligations, service standards, lifecycle exposure and cost allocation

assumptions.

• Challenge cost assumptions where opportunities exist to improve efficiency, affordability or value for money.

• Support integrated planning through clear visibility of operational expenditure, lifecycle obligations and recovery

opportunities.

• Promote alignment between operational sustainability objectives and cost recovery strategies.

5. Financial Assurance and Cost Recovery Performance

• Maintain a consolidated city-wide view of operational costs, service charge assumptions, recovery methodologies and

cost allocation structures.

• Review cost recovery performance and identify variances, risks, affordability issues, recovery gaps and potential revenue

leakage.

• Coordinate assurance activities relating to service charge calculations, allocation methodologies and recovery

assumptions.

• Provide recommendations to improve transparency, accountability and effectiveness of cost recovery arrangements.

• Support leadership reporting on cost recovery performance, service charge outcomes and operational affordability

pressures.

• Monitor trends, exceptions and performance indicators to identify emerging risks and improvement opportunities.

• Ensure service charge arrangements remain sustainable and support long-term operational and financial objectives.

• Develop governance reporting and performance dashboards covering cost recovery effectiveness and financial resilience.

6. District, Operator and Stakeholder Interface

• Build strong working relationships with districts, operators, City Operations, Asset Management, Finance and governance

stakeholders.

• Coordinate stakeholder engagement activities associated with service charges, revenue generation and cost recovery

initiatives.

Facilitate discussions on operating assumptions, service levels, allocation methodologies, charging structures and

recovery mechanisms.

• Ensure district and operator requirements are captured, reviewed and appropriately reflected within service charge

governance arrangements.

• Support resolution of service charge and cost allocation issues through structured engagement, analysis and

recommendations.

• Promote transparency and understanding of charging methodologies and governance requirements across stakeholders.

• Support senior leadership engagement on financially significant recovery, charging and revenue matters.

• Facilitate cross-functional reviews of emerging operational, commercial and cost recovery challenges.

7. Consultant and Commercial Management

• Define scopes, deliverables, acceptance criteria and performance requirements for consultants supporting service charge

and revenue initiatives.

• Manage consultant activities, outputs, recommendations and reporting requirements.

• Review benchmarking studies, financial assessments, charge methodologies, governance recommendations and

commercial evaluations.

• Ensure consultant outputs are evidence-based, practical and aligned with Estate Management objectives.

• Coordinate independent reviews and specialist assessments as required to support decision making.

• Escalate significant findings, risks, opportunities and recommendations to senior management where appropriate.

• Ensure consultant recommendations are translated into practical governance improvements and decision-support

outputs.

• Promote effective knowledge transfer and capability development through external specialist engagements.

8. Continuous Improvement, Benchmarking and Reporting

• Promote continual improvement of service charge governance, cost recovery methodologies and revenue opportunity

assessment processes.

• Coordinate benchmarking exercises through specialist consultants to compare service charge practices, cost recovery

arrangements and revenue opportunities against relevant market comparators.

• Monitor industry developments, regulatory changes, operational trends and emerging practices that may impact service

charge or revenue strategies.

• Develop dashboards, management reports and executive briefings covering service charge performance, revenue

opportunities and recovery effectiveness.

• Review governance effectiveness and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, transparency and value creation.

• Support the development of Estate Management capability through guidance, workshops, governance routines and

stakeholder engagement.

• Maintain lessons learned and continuous improvement processes for service charge and revenue management activities.

• Promote evidence-based decision making through high-quality reporting and performance analysis.

Requirements

Experience

• Minimum 15 years of progressive experience in service charges, commercial management, cost recovery, financial

planning, real estate operations, asset management, infrastructure operations or related disciplines, including senior leadership experience.

• Proven experience developing, managing or governing service charge models and cost allocation methodologies within

complex multi-stakeholder environments.

• Experience evaluating revenue opportunities, commercial initiatives, cost recovery strategies and financial sustainability

programs.

• Experience coordinating operational, asset management and finance stakeholders to develop evidence-based

commercial recommendations.

• Experience managing consultants, specialist advisors and commercial studies.

• Experience supporting executive-level decision making through financial modelling, governance reporting and commercial

analysis.

• Experience within large-scale destinations, cities, infrastructure programs, mixed-use developments, public realm

environments or giga-projects is strongly preferred.

Preferred Background

• Background in service charge governance, estate management, property management, commercial management,

infrastructure finance, revenue optimization or operational finance.

• Practical exposure to city operations, asset management, operational readiness, lifecycle planning and cost recovery

environments.

• Experience working across finance, operations, asset management and governance functions to support sustainable

operating models and commercial outcomes.

Technical & Functional Expectations

• Service charge governance, allocation methodologies and cost recovery frameworks.

• Financial analysis, business case development and commercial evaluation.

• Revenue opportunity identification, assessment and value optimization.

• Operating expenditure analysis and stakeholder coordination.

• Lifecycle cost integration and long-term operational sustainability considerations.

• Benchmarking, assurance reviews, performance reporting and governance controls.

• Consultant management, commercial oversight and executive-level reporting.

• Cross-functional stakeholder engagement and complex decision support.

Education

• Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Real Estate, Asset Management, Business Administration,

Commercial Management or a related discipline.

• Master's degree in a relevant discipline is preferred.

• Professional certification or membership in finance, service charge management, commercial management, asset

management, real estate or business management is desirable.

Partner with the best

title: Fractional Chief Medical Officer
description:
At the forefront of health tech innovation, CopilotIQ+Biofourmis is transforming in-home care with the industry's first AI-driven platform that supports individuals through every stage of their health journey-from pre-surgical optimization to acute, post-acute and chronic care. We are helping people live healthier, longer lives by bringing personalized, proactive care directly into their homes. With CopilotIQ's commitment to enhancing the lives of seniors with chronic conditions and Biofourmis' advanced data-driven insights and virtual care solutions, we're setting a new standard in accessible healthcare. If you're passionate about driving real change in healthcare, join the CopilotIQ+Biofourmis Team!

What is the Fractional Chief Medical Officer role?

We are looking for an exceptional clinical leader with the credibility and sophistication to lead among their clinical peers, while bringing a forward-looking vision for the evolution and future of our clinical offerings.

The Fractional Chief Medical Officer (CMO) serves as the senior clinical leader supporting commercial growth and strategic partnerships along with clinical product strategy. This role partners closely with Sales, Product, Clinical Operations, and Executive Leadership to articulate the clinical value of our platform to payors, health systems, and strategic partners, while collaborating with Product leadership to drive clinical innovation and establish a robust framework for measuring and demonstrating clinical outcomes.

Unlike a traditional CMO role, this position is primarily externally facing, helping prospective customers understand the evidence, clinical workflows, quality outcomes, and regulatory considerations behind our chronic conditions management programs. This person also has a strong vision for how the product could evolve to continually drive improvements in clinical outcomes.

The ideal candidate is equally comfortable discussing clinical evidence with physician leaders, presenting ROI models to payor executives and advising product teams on future clinical capabilities.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Serve as the clinical executive during enterprise sales discussions with health plans and risk-bearing organizations.
  • Present the clinical strategy, care model, evidence base, and expected outcomes of our hypertension, diabetes, and CHF programs.
  • Build credibility with Chief Medical Officers, Medical Directors, Population Health, Quality and Stars leaders, and Quality executives.
  • Support RFP responses, finalist presentations, and executive briefings.
  • Partner with Sales to address clinical objections and differentiate our platform from competitors.
  • Represent the company at industry conferences, payer forums, and customer events.
  • Drive the publication of research that demonstrably proves the outsized savings we are driving for our payor partners.

What you’ll bring:

  • MD with unrestricted U.S. medical license
  • Board Certification in Internal Medicine, Cardiology, Endocrinology, or a related specialty.
  • 10+ years of clinical leadership experience.
  • Knowledge of CMS Stars, HEDIS, NCQA, and quality improvement programs.
  • Experience working with Medicare Advantage populations.
  • Deep understanding of hypertension, diabetes, and congestive heart failure management.
  • Experience presenting to executive healthcare audiences.
  • Strong understanding of value-based care, quality programs, and population health.

title: Senior Program Manager
description:
Overview

DecisionPoint Corporation is seeking an experienced Senior Technical Program Manager (TPM) to lead a multi-year enterprise IT modernization, software development, cloud transformation, and sustainment effort supporting a high-visibility Department of Defense (DoD) program. The Senior Technical Program Manager will provide strategic technical leadership and operational oversight across all Task Order activities, including Agile software development, DevSecOps implementation, AWS GovCloud deployment, cybersecurity and RMF compliance, systems integration, UI/UX modernization, data migration, training, and enterprise support services. The TPM will serve as the principal technical liaison to Government stakeholders, guiding architecture, delivery strategy, technical execution, and modernization initiatives while ensuring alignment with contractual requirements and mission objectives. This position is fully remote.

Duties & Responsibilities

  • Lead all phases of program execution, including planning, technical delivery, monitoring, and successful completion of contractual and mission objectives.
  • Manage program cost, schedule, risk, quality, and technical performance for a complex, multi-phase, cost-reimbursable contract.
  • Provide leadership to cross-functional teams supporting software engineering, DevSecOps, cloud infrastructure, cybersecurity, data management, training, and help desk operations.
  • Drive enterprise modernization efforts, including cloud adoption, application modernization, systems integration, and digital transformation initiatives.
  • Coordinate with Government stakeholders, support contractors, and technical teams to ensure successful delivery of capabilities and services.
  • Promote Agile and DevSecOps best practices, including sprint planning, backlog prioritization, CI/CD enablement, iterative development, and continuous improvement.
  • Track and report performance metrics, deliverable status, quality objectives, risks, and customer feedback through Monthly Status Reports (MSRs), Technical Status Meetings, and executive briefings.
  • Oversee development and execution of key program deliverables, including the Project Management Plan (PMP), Quality Management Plan (QMP), DevSecOps Plan, Transition Plan, Cybersecurity Documentation, and Go-Live Plan.
  • Ensure compliance with DoD cybersecurity, RMF, cloud security, and software delivery requirements.
  • Champion innovation and continual service improvement across the platform and supporting operational processes.

Qualifications

  • Active Secret clearance required.
  • Bachelor's degree in business, management, information systems, computer science, engineering, or another field related to work under this requirement.
  • Minimum of nine (9) years of experience leading technology, software development, cybersecurity, cloud modernization, or enterprise IT programs of similar scope and complexity.
  • Project Management Professional (PMP) or Program Management Professional (PgMP) certification required.
  • Demonstrated experience leading large, cross-functional technical teams responsible for software engineering, cloud infrastructure, cybersecurity, DevSecOps, data management, and IT operations.
  • Strong leadership and stakeholder engagement skills with the ability to communicate complex technical concepts to executive, operational, and technical audiences.
  • Experience managing Agile software delivery efforts, including roadmap planning, release management, backlog prioritization, and iterative development methodologies.
  • Demonstrated success supporting DoD or Federal programs involving enterprise modernization, cloud transformation, cybersecurity compliance, or digital services.
  • Experience managing cost-reimbursable contracts and operating within Federal acquisition environments.
Desired
  • Minimum of eight (8) years of experience leading transformative IT/DevSecOps initiatives and championing end-to-end modern iterative software development solutions.
  • Experience designing, implementing, or overseeing DevSecOps pipelines, automated testing, CI/CD processes, and secure software delivery practices.
  • Experience deploying and managing solutions within AWS GovCloud or comparable secure cloud environments.
  • Experience developing and standardizing business rules, workflows, and operational processes across interagency or intra-agency systems.
  • Experience supporting enterprise application modernization, cloud migration, system integration, and digital transformation initiatives.
  • Familiarity with DoD cybersecurity requirements, Risk Management Framework (RMF), Zero Trust principles, and secure cloud operations.
  • Possess one or more of the following certifications:
    • EC-Council Certified Chief Information Security Officer (C|CISO)
    • SANS Global Security Leadership Certification (GSLC)
    • ISC2 Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP)
    • ISACA Certified Information Systems Manager (CISM)
    • CompTIA Advanced Security Practitioner (CASP+)
Preferred Certifications
  • SAFe Program Consultant (SPC), SAFe Agilist (SA), Certified Scrum Professional (CSP), Certified Scrum Master (CSM), or equivalent Agile certification.
  • AWS Certified Solutions Architect, AWS Security Specialty, AWS Advanced Networking, or equivalent cloud certification.
  • ITIL v4 Foundation, Managing Professional, or Strategic Leader certification.

Our Equal Employment Opportunity Policy

  • EEO and Affirmative Action Policy: DecisionPoint Corporation is an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. It is the policy of DecisionPoint Corporation to provide equal employment opportunity in accordance with all applicable Equal Employment Opportunity/Affirmative Action laws, directives and regulations to all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability status, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other protected status under Federal, State or Local laws.
  • Pay Transparency Policy: In accordance with Presidential Executive Order 13665, DecisionPoint Corporation will not discharge or in any other manner discriminate against employees or applicants because they have inquired about, discussed, or disclosed their own pay or the pay of another employee or applicant. However, employees who have access to the compensation information of other employees or applicants as a part of their essential job functions cannot disclose the pay of other employees or applicants to individuals who do not otherwise have access to compensation information, unless the disclosure is (a) in response to a formal complaint or charge, (b) in furtherance of an investigation, proceeding, hearing, or action, including an investigation conducted by the employer, or (c) consistent with the contractor's legal duty to furnish information.
  • Authorization to Share Resume and Personal Information: By expressing your interest and submitting your resume for this position, you authorize DecisionPoint Corporation to share your resume, as well as personal information included on the resume, with its subsidiaries, affiliates and teaming partners for the purpose of considering you for this position and other available positions requiring comparable skills, education and experience. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year.

The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.

The Opportunity:

Flexport IT is looking for a Senior Systems Engineer (Identity & Access). In this role, you will design, implement, and administer our Identity and Access Management (IAM) solutions to ensure secure, efficient user lifecycle management.

While you are our resident Okta expert, you are also a high-level IT generalist. You will oversee our broader SaaS ecosystem (Google Workspace, Slack, Jira) and endpoint management infrastructure (Jamf, Intune). Your expertise will drive automation, protect sensitive data, mitigate security risks, and maintain compliance in a heavily regulated industry.

You will continually strive towards automation of toil. If you are still manually doing the same operational tasks 18 months from now, something has gone wrong. Flexport’s book of business is growing fast, but the promise of technology is that we can grow our business faster than our headcount. The automation you build will be a key factor in that effort.

You Will

  • IAM Architecture: Design, implement, and maintain the end-to-end lifecycle of Identity and Access Management platforms.
  • Okta & Directory Trust: Administer Okta, directory services, Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), and advanced password management.
  • SaaS Operations: Manage core collaboration tools including Google Workspace, Microsoft O365, Slack, and Jira/Confluence.
  • Unified Endpoint Management: Oversee our global fleet of Mac and Windows devices using Jamf and MS Intune.
  • Lifecycle Automation: Build automated workflows for provisioning, deprovisioning, and application access.
  • Identity Governance: Establish role-based access control (RBAC), entitlement reviews, and access certification processes.
  • SSO Integration: Lead the technical onboarding of new SaaS applications for Single Sign-On (SSO).
  • Security Partnership: Collaborate closely with the Security team to embed security best practices into our IT infrastructure.
  • Documentation & Roadmaps: Author technical operating procedures, engineering roadmaps, and compliance policies.
  • Operations Support: Provide high-tier technical leadership and escalation support for complex IT operations.

You Should Have

  • Experience: 5+ years of experience in IAM systems engineering paired with broad IT infrastructure management.
  • Okta Expertise: Deep, hands-on mastery of Okta configuration, policy creation, and application integration.
  • Core Protocols: Strong knowledge of IAM standards including SAML, SCIM, OAuth, OIDC, IGA, RBAC, and LDAP.
  • Automation Skills: Experience with scripting (e.g., Python, Bash, or PowerShell) and Okta Workflows to automate IT tasks.
  • SaaS & Endpoint Ecosystem: Proven track record managing Google Workspace, Slack, Jira, Jamf (macOS), and Intune (Windows).
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, a related field, or equivalent practical engineering experience.
  • Compliance Mindset: A "compliance-first" attitude to navigate the rigorous requirements of a heavily regulated industry.
  • Soft Skills: Excellent problem-solving abilities paired with strong collaborative and interpersonal communication.

title: Recycling Services Driver
description:
Facilities Maintenance Operations (FMO), offers primary building maintenance, landscape, fire safety, custodial, recycling, and event support services to Harvard schools and departments on a fee-for-service basis. Position Description:

  • The Recycling and Waste Pickup Driver is responsible for the safe and efficient collection, transportation, and handling of recycling, compost, solid waste, universal waste, and surplus furniture from designated campus locations.
  • This position operates commercial vehicles, including recycling and waste collection trucks and box trucks, services compactors and dumpsters, and supports campus waste diversion and surplus property removal programs.
  • The role ensures materials are collected in accordance with established routes, schedules, environmental requirements, and safety procedures while delivering reliable service to campus customers and departments.

Job-Specific Responsibilities:

  • Operate commercial vehicles in a safe and efficient manner, including rear-load trucks, roll-off trucks, box trucks, and other assigned vehicles.
  • Collect and transport recycling, compost, solid waste, and other designated material streams from campus buildings, loading docks, outdoor collection areas, and other service locations.
  • Perform campus pickups of universal waste, including lamps, batteries, and electronic waste, and transport materials to designated storage or disposal locations in accordance with departmental procedures and environmental regulations.
  • Perform pickups and transportation of surplus furniture and other reusable or surplus materials from campus departments and buildings using a box truck or other assigned vehicle.
  • Service dumpsters, compactors, toters, and other waste and recycling containers according to established routes and schedules.
  • Load, unload, move, and secure furniture, equipment, containers, pallets, and other materials safely by hand or with material handling equipment.
  • Perform daily pre-trip and post-trip inspections of assigned vehicles and complete all required inspection reports and documentation.
  • Monitor vehicle and equipment performance and promptly report mechanical issues, damage, safety concerns, or needed repairs.
  • Ensure all loads are properly secured and transported in compliance with local, state, federal, and University requirements.
  • Maintain cleanliness of collection areas by picking up loose debris and ensuring containers are returned to their proper locations after service.
  • Identify contamination issues in recycling and compost streams and report recurring problems to supervisors.
  • Handle universal waste materials in accordance with departmental procedures, environmental health and safety requirements, and applicable regulations.
  • Communicate professionally with building occupants, campus departments, dispatch, and supervisors regarding service requests, access issues, scheduling, and special pickups.

  • Follow all Department of Transportation, OSHA, environmental, University, and departmental safety rules, policies, and procedures.
  • Operate hydraulic systems, liftgates, compactors, cart tippers, pallet jacks, hand trucks, and other related equipment safely and properly.

Working Conditions:

  • Critical Operations Personnel: This position is designated as Critical Operations Personnel and is required to provide on-site support during emergency situations as determined by management.

Physical Requirements:

Requires the ability to:

  • sit, stand, walk, bend, lift, push, pull, and climb throughout the workday.
  • lift and move materials, furniture, containers, and other items weighing up to 50 pounds on a regular basis, and heavier items with assistance or material handling equipment.
  • climb in and out of trucks repeatedly during the shift.

  • Ability to work independently, follow established routes, and adapt to changing operational needs.
  • Strong attention to safety, reliability, and customer service.

  • Knowledge of safe vehicle operation, backing procedures, and load securement practices.

title: Senior Security Engineer
description:
Join Us, and Ship Robots

Weave was founded to build the robots we’d want to have in our own home. We believe the next generation of robotics will transform everyday life by enabling people to do more and to reclaim time to spend on what’s important.

We also believe robots are in a sense like any other product: to matter, they have to ship. Our robots are already operating in real homes and businesses, giving us the opportunity to rapidly improve from real-world experience. With a growing team, strong customer demand, and capital for expansion, we’re entering an exciting stage of growth—and we’re looking for people with exceptional talent and standards to help bring home robotics to millions of households.

The Role

At Weave, we’re building robots designed to operate in the most personal environment there is: the home. Our robots combine cameras, sensors, actuators, embedded compute, cloud infrastructure, and consumer applications into a deeply integrated system—and earning our customers’ trust requires making security a fundamental part of that system from the beginning.

As a Senior Security Engineer, you’ll work on security and system integrity across the full surface area of our product, from embedded devices and robot software to cloud infrastructure, APIs, mobile applications, and fleet operations. You’ll work directly with engineers to threat-model new systems, find vulnerabilities, design secure architectures, and build the infrastructure that protects robots already operating in the real world. This is a highly hands-on role: you’ll help define our long-term security strategy while remaining close enough to the product to inspect code, probe systems, investigate incidents, and ship fixes yourself.

Responsibilities

  • Own product security: Define and continuously improve the security architecture of our robots, applications, backend services, and supporting infrastructure.

  • Threat modeling & secure design: Lead threat modeling and security reviews for new hardware and software capabilities, identifying remote and physical attack surfaces and designing mitigations before systems reach production.

  • Robot & embedded security: Secure device identity, boot and update chains, firmware, embedded Linux systems, and hardware interfaces.

  • Cloud & application security: Identify and mitigate vulnerabilities across cloud infrastructure, APIs, authentication systems, web services, and iOS/Android applications.

  • Security testing: Perform code review, penetration testing, vulnerability research, and adversarial testing across our product stack. Develop tooling that makes security testing increasingly automated.

  • Detection & incident response: Build logging, monitoring, detection, and incident-response capabilities that allow us to rapidly identify, investigate, contain, and remediate security events.

  • Raise the security bar: Establish practical security standards and processes, educate engineers, and build a culture where security is owned across the engineering organization.

What You'll Bring

  • Product security expertise: 4+ years securing connected products, embedded systems, robotics, IoT, autonomous systems, or other physical platforms, with experience reasoning across hardware, firmware, embedded Linux, operating systems, networks, cloud services, and applications.

  • Linux & systems security: Strong understanding of Linux security boundaries, processes, permissions, networking, containers, system hardening, and common privilege-escalation techniques.

  • Application security: Experience finding and mitigating vulnerabilities across APIs, backend services, web or mobile applications, including familiarity with OWASP Top 10 and modern application security practices.

  • Software engineering: Strong programming ability in Python, C++, Go, Rust, or similar languages, with the ability to reason about production code and build security tooling yourself.

  • Security testing: Hands-on experience with source-code review, SAST/DAST, dependency analysis, fuzzing, penetration testing, and security tools such as Burp Suite, Semgrep, CodeQL, Ghidra, or similar.

  • Threat modeling: Experience using structured approaches such as STRIDE, attack trees, or similar methodologies to reason about complex systems and drive architectural improvements.

  • Incident response: Experience investigating security incidents, analyzing logs and telemetry, performing root-cause analysis, and driving remediation.

Nice to Have

  • Networking depth: Familiarity with Ethernet, Wi-Fi, TCP/IP, and common network protocols, including experience using Wireshark, tcpdump, or similar packet-analysis tools to diagnose networking and security issues.

  • Security standards: Familiarity with security standards and guidance relevant to connected consumer products, such as NIST IR 8259, NIST SSDF, UL 2900, or similar.

  • Connected-device security: Experience with device provisioning, PKI/mTLS, device identity, signed OTA updates, credential rotation/revocation, and fleet-scale secrets management.

The Critical Facilities Technician supports the safe, reliable operation of mission-critical data center infrastructure in a 24/7 environment. This role is responsible for monitoring, operating, maintaining, and documenting electrical, mechanical, and building systems across day, swing, and night shifts while following approved procedures, safety standards, and escalation protocols.

Job Description

  • Operate, monitor, and maintain critical electrical and mechanical infrastructure, including UPS systems, generators, switchgear, PDUs, CRAC/CRAH units, and related equipment.
  • Use BMS, EPMS, and DCIM platforms to monitor system performance, identify alarms, and respond promptly to abnormal operating conditions.
  • Complete preventive and corrective maintenance tasks according to approved maintenance schedules, procedures, and documentation requirements.
  • Execute Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Methods of Procedure (MOPs), and Emergency Operating Procedures (EOPs) accurately and consistently.
  • Troubleshoot equipment issues, support incident response, and escalate conditions that may affect uptime, safety, or service continuity.
  • Coordinate and oversee vendor work to confirm activities are completed safely, professionally, and in accordance with approved procedures.
  • Maintain accurate shift logs, equipment readings, maintenance records, and incident documentation.
  • Follow all site safety requirements, including lockout/tagout (LOTO), electrical safety, arc flash, and OSHA-related procedures.
  • Perform routine rounds, inspections, and equipment checks to verify proper operation and identify potential issues before they affect service.
  • Support commissioning, testing, and minor project work as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 2–5 years of experience in data center operations, critical facilities, industrial maintenance, or a related technical environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working in a live data center, hospital, utility, manufacturing, or other mission-critical environment.
  • Hands-on experience with UPS systems, generators, switchgear, HVAC equipment, or building automation systems.
  • Certifications such as CDCTP, CDCP, OSHA 10/30, electrical safety, HVAC, or other relevant technical credentials.
  • Experience supporting commissioning, integrated systems testing, or emergency response drills.

Working knowledge of electrical, mechanical, HVAC, and fire/life safety systems used in critical environments.

Ability to use monitoring platforms such as BMS, EPMS, or DCIM to review system status and respond to alerts.

Ability to read and interpret basic electrical one-line diagrams, equipment manuals, and technical procedures.

Strong troubleshooting, communication, and problem-solving skills.

Familiarity with applicable safety and industry standards, including NFPA, NEC,

OSHA, and site-specific procedures.

Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a shift-based operations environment.

Willingness and ability to work day, swing, or night shifts, including weekends, holidays, and overtime as needed.

Relevant technical training, trade experience, military experience, or equivalent hands-on experience in facilities operations.

title: Senior data engineer
description:
The Senior Data & ML Engineer is responsible for executing the technical implementation of the Data Transformation. The role focuses on designing and building the data ingestion and processing platform, including automated data pipelines, an integrated database, cross-functional system integrations and AI/ ML-ready data structures.

The Senior Data & ML Engineer must translate strategic direction into concrete technical solutions, make sound architectural recommendations, and deliver scalable, robust, production-grade data capabilities that support reliable reporting, advanced analytics and machine learning use cases across the business.

This role will form part of our technical shared services team, contributing to the development of digital management systems, O&M projects implementations and ongoing development within the Data Transformation Project.

Key Responsibilities

Design, build and maintain end-to-end automated data pipelines from internal and external sources into a central data platform:

Develop an integrated and scalable Single Source of Truth (SSOT) database, consolidating data from ERP, OT/Io T, Share Point ensuring scalable data flows. Develop modular and scalable data ingestion developing API integrations, SQL Stored Procedures and ETL frameworks, maintaining reliable, automated data ingestion between internal and external platforms to the SSOT database. Own end to end data development solutions.

Design and develop scalable data models (staging, core, marts, feature sets) that support strategic reporting, advanced analytics and ML.

Design scalable data models across clearly defined layers, including staging (raw landed data), core (cleaned and standardised single source of truth), marts (business-ready views for specific domains), and feature sets (model-ready tables for machine learning and advanced analytics). Implement MLOps practices (versioning of data and models, CI/CD for models, monitoring, retraining strategies) as ML use cases mature. Own end-to-end development and processing (data algorithms and ML solutions) Ensure all data models, pipelines and storage approaches are AI/ML-ready.

Technical platform development, data orchestration and data management

Apply and enforce data management, security and governance standards in line with the Data Governance Policy. Implement structured change management (version control, release processes, approvals, rollback plans). Work with divisional data owners to reduce data silos, standardise data flows and ensure adherence to agreed standards and timelines.

Asset Lifecycle Management & Platform Integration

Oversee the full onboarding and offboarding process for company assets and equipment within the central asset management platforms. Ensure seamless data integration by validating that all asset information is correctly captured and synchronized. Maintain data integrity and platform compliance by routinely reviewing asset entries, resolving discrepancies. Skills and Competencies ETL/ELT orchestration and job scheduling (Automated workflows) Data modelling (staging, core, marts, feature sets); production operations (monitoring, alerting, incident response) Strong SQL; proficiency in Python for data engineering and ML-enabling tasks; and solid programming foundations in Python, SQL and/ or C# Ability to make scalable architectural decisions and prepare data for ML and model integration into workflows. Solid ML foundations (feature engineering, evaluation, overfitting, drift) and ability to design data pipelines that are fit for ML.

Senior, hands‑on engineering mindset; comfortable owning technical direction.

Proven ability to design and lead data platform or data product builds. Self‑directed and proactive: identifies problems, proposes solutions and drives implementation without detailed step‑by‑step direction. Clear, structured communication skills. can explain technical options and trade‑offs to non‑technical stakeholders and leadership.

Strong systems thinking and architecture skills: designs for scalability, maintainability and AI/ML-readiness from the outset.

Strong engineering discipline: version control, testing, deployment processes, documentation and incident handling. Enjoys building automation, integrations and ML‑ready datasets. Cross‑team coordination and influence – able to work with multiple divisions, follow up with stakeholders and enforce agreed standards and timelines. Experience, Knowledge and Qualifications Degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Mathematics or a related field. Proficient in data engineering. 5+ years in data engineering/ data platform development at a senior/ lead level. Programming foundations in Python, SQL and/or C#. Hands‑on responsibility for API integration (REST/JSON, auth, pagination, error handling); ETL/ELT orchestration and job scheduling; data modelling (staging, core, marts/ feature sets); and production operations (monitoring, alerting, incident response). Strong SQL skills (DDL/DML, performance tuning, stored procedures, views, functions). Proficiency in Python for data engineering and ML-enabling tasks, plus experience with ETL. Strong foundations in ML concepts and practical experience preparing data for ML and integrating models into data workflows (even if not a pure data scientist). Advantageous: Hands‑on experience with ML models in production (e.g. forecasting, classification, anomaly detection) and associated MLOps tooling. Exposure to neural networks/ deep learning (e.g. Tensor Flow, Py Torch) and modern ML pipelines. Design and support workflow automation and lightweight data applications using tools such as Power Apps and Power Automate, integrating these solutions with the core data platform to enable efficient business processes. Experience with data lakes/ big data architectures and orchestration tools (e.g. Airflow, Prefect, Azure Data Factory or similar). Familiarity with AI/ ML governance, model risk and secure data handling. Experience working with industrial/Io T or energy sector data.

description:

In addition, you will be paired with a dedicated mentor who will empower you to take ownership of your work and make a difference.

As a Graduate Software Engineer, you will work closely with best-in-class traders, researchers, risk analysts and other engineers to develop simple, well-architected solutions that meet the needs of our business. No one day is ever the same. You will gain and develop in-depth knowledge of engineering for the capital markets. Our collective passion to solve problems makes a direct impact on our business.

You’ll join a culture of collaboration and excellence, where you’ll be surrounded by curious thinkers and creative problem solvers. Motivated by a passion for continuous improvement, you’ll thrive in a supportive, high-performing environment alongside talented colleagues, working collectively to tackle the toughest problems in the financial markets.

In addition, you’ll receive:

  • The opportunity to work alongside best-in-class professionals

  • 27 paid vacation days plus all UK public holidays

  • Daily breakfast and lunch, along with support on commuting expenses

  • Private medical insurance, pension scheme, and ClassPass fitness membership

  • Training and continuous learning opportunities

  • International transfer opportunities for global career growth

Who you are

  • Passionate about clean code, simple, well-architected systems, and continuous improvement

  • A solid grasp of algorithms, memory and concurrency models, CPU-architecture, operating systems and relational databases

title: Automation Controls Engineer
description:
Application close date:

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.

About Blue Origin

Blue Origin is a spaceflight and exploration company founded on the belief that humanity's future depends on our ability to live and work in space. We are working to lower the cost of access to space through reusable launch vehicles and in-space systems, enabling a future where millions of people live and work in space. We value curiosity, passion, integrity, and a relentless drive to achieve our mission. Blue Origin is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

About This Role

Blue Origin's Factory Automation team is part of the Advanced Manufacturing organization within Operations — serving as the in-house automation integrator responsible for designing, building, and deploying the custom equipment and systems that enable scalable, repeatable production across Blue Origin's manufacturing business units. We build manufacturing capability from the ground up, developing automated solutions that directly drive the delivery of Blue Origin's products across current and future programs.

We are looking for an Automation Controls Engineer who brings hands-on experience in industrial controls design and automation systems integration. This role spans R&D, design, build, installation, and commissioning — offering the opportunity to grow your technical depth and ownership across the full project lifecycle. We are looking for engineers who understand the why behind the systems they build — who can reason from physics and engineering fundamentals, diagnose problems at their root, and architect sound solutions to novel challenges. If you are the kind of engineer who reaches for first principles before reaching for a manual, this team is built for you.

Responsibilities

  • Collaborate with applications engineers on conceptual automated manufacturing equipment, contributing controls architecture input from concept through detailed design

  • Design and support control system architectures including network topology, I/O distribution, safety systems, and communication protocols

  • Participate in the industrial controls and electrical design of bespoke automation systems

  • Apply engineering first principles to analyze system behavior, identify root causes, and develop technically sound solutions to novel automation challenges

  • Develop offline simulations of automated systems to validate control logic, robot paths, cycle times, and system behavior prior to hardware availability

  • Support and execute online debugging and commissioning of PLC, HMI, robot, and similar industrial controls programs

  • Integrate auxiliary equipment, machines, and tools into unified control systems

  • Work with panel fabricators and field installation teams; provide technical support during system integration and commissioning

  • Support and lead factory and site acceptance testing, and contribute to the build, installation, commissioning, and start-up of automated manufacturing systems

  • Create controls documentation packages including sequence of operations, I/O lists, network diagrams, and program documentation

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree or higher in Electrical, Mechanical, Mechatronics, Controls, or related engineering field

  • Minimum 2 years of hands-on experience developing or integrating industrial controls and automation systems, including PLC and HMI programming as core competencies

  • Exposure to one or more industrial automation platforms such as robots, material handling systems (gantries, AGVs, conveyors), CNC machine integration, NDT, assembly, testing, or process tools (torque, welding, grinding, or similar) — breadth across all areas is not expected

  • Demonstrated ability to interpret and review electrical and mechanical drawings

  • Experience with industrial safety system design including functional safety devices, safety PLCs, and safety-rated circuits

  • Must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum

Preferred Qualifications

  • Familiarity with industrial automation and machine safety standards including IEC 61131, ANSI B11, NFPA 79, RIA R15.06, and functional safety standards (IEC 62061 / ISO 13849)

  • Experience with industrial automation simulation software for offline programming or virtual commissioning, such as Plant Simulate, Process Simulate, Visual Components, KUKA.Sim, RobotStudio, or similar

  • Experience with industrial machine vision systems, including configuration or application development using platforms such as Cognex

  • Experience building, modifying, or troubleshooting electrical control panels

  • Experience with electrical design for industrial control systems using AutoCAD Electrical, EPLAN, or similar electrical CAD platforms

  • Demonstrated history of delivering custom automated manufacturing systems from concept through production ramp-up

  • Demonstrated ability to apply engineering fundamentals — including mechanics, electronics, and control theory — to diagnose complex system failures and develop first-principles solutions in novel or undefined problem spaces

Don't have all the listed qualifications? Blue Origin is committed to building a diverse team. If you meet the basic qualifications and are excited about this role, we encourage you to apply.


Base Pay Range for:

CO applicants is $123,714.00 - $173,199.60

Other site ranges may differ

Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway.   • Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical

Benefits

  • Benefits include: Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
  • Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)
  • Paid Time Off: Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays.
  • Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company's intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company's results, or other factors at the company's sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details.

title: Transport Coordinator
description:
We are looking for a Transport Coordinator to join our team in Denmark. The successful candidate will be responsible for coordinating daily transport activities and ensuring that drivers, vehicles, customers, and deliveries are properly organized.

Key Responsibilities

  • Plan and coordinate daily driving schedules.

  • Coordinate with drivers and assign transportation tasks.

  • Monitor ongoing tasks and transportation activities.

  • Help in driving self during shortage of driver.

  • Communicate with customers, drivers, and transport partners.

  • Handle changes, delays, and other transportation-related issues.

  • Prepare and maintain transport schedules and documentation.

  • Register and follow up on completed trips and deliveries.

  • Ensure that transportation activities are carried out efficiently and on time.

  • Assist with general administrative tasks related to transportation.

Requirements

  • Good organizational and communication skills.

  • Ability to coordinate several tasks at the same time.

  • Previous experience in transport, logistics, dispatching, or administration.

  • Driving experience is also an advantage.

  • Good knowledge of computers and basic office software.

  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

  • Good English communication skills. Danish is an advantage.

We Offer

  • A stable and professional working environment.

  • Full-time employment.

  • Competitive salary according to qualifications and experience.

  • Opportunities for professional development.

  • A responsible and varied position within the transport industry.

Jobannonce – Transportkoordinator

Vi søger en transportkoordinator til vores team i Danmark. Den rette kandidat skal være ansvarlig for koordinering af den daglige transport og sikre, at chauffører, køretøjer, kunder og kørsler er godt organiseret.

Arbejdsopgaver

  • Planlægge og koordinere den daglige kørsel.

  • Koordinere med chauffører og fordele transportopgaver.

  • Følge op på igangværende opgaver og transportaktiviteter.

  • Hjælpe med selv at køre ved mangel på chauffører.

  • Kommunikere med kunder, chauffører og transportpartnere.

  • Håndtere ændringer, forsinkelser og andre transportrelaterede problemer.

  • Udarbejde og vedligeholde kørselsplaner og relevant dokumentation.

  • Registrere og følge op på gennemførte kørsler og leverancer.

  • Sikre, at transportopgaverne udføres effektivt og til tiden.

  • Hjælpe med generelle administrative opgaver relateret til transport.

Kvalifikationer

  • Gode organisatoriske og kommunikative evner.

  • Evne til at koordinere flere opgaver samtidig.

  • Tidligere erfaring inden for transport, logistik, disponering eller administration.

  • Kørsels- og chaufførerfaring er en fordel.

  • Gode IT-kundskaber og kendskab til almindelige kontorprogrammer.

  • Evne til at arbejde selvstændigt og samtidig indgå i et team.

  • Gode engelskkundskaber. Dansk er en fordel.

Vi tilbyder

  • Et stabilt og professionelt arbejdsmiljø.

  • Fuldtidsansættelse.

  • Konkurrencedygtig løn efter kvalifikationer og erfaring.

  • Mulighed for faglig udvikling.

  • En ansvarsfuld og varieret stilling inden for transportbranchen.
